text:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: release/2026-03-15. Canary fraction=5% -> region=eu-west. :rocket:

alex.k: seeing spike in 5xx and latency on canary instances, started ~1762104300, hitting api-generation and embed endpoints

alex.k: logs: `504 gateway timeout` and `context deadline exceeded` from worker pool\\n\nalex.k: sample log tail:
```
[03-15T12:05:02Z] worker-23 generation request timed out after 8s
[03-15T12:05:03Z] kv-cache miss, falling back to full model load
[03-15T12:05:04Z] 504 upstream
```
\ntera: @tara here, oncall taking a look. Paging follow-up in 2m if not resolved\

tara: alex, can you confirm if this is only canary or also prod traffic routed?

alex.k: only canary pool, traffic steer toggled to 5% as expected. But canary nodes are getting backpressured leading to queue growth on router

ops-sre: I'm watching the router queue metrics — queue depth jumped x6 in eu-west canary subpool, latency p95 up to 3.2s

infra-bot: Deploy rollback check: previous stable image tag=release/2026-03-08-rc2, canary tag=release/2026-03-15. Compatible rollback? yes (feature flags allow)

jm: recommend killing the feature-flag for the new batching optimizer first, lower blast radius. If that doesn't help, prepare to kill the canary or rollback.

alex.k: ack. running kill-switch now: `rfctl ff set batching_optimizer_enabled=false --env=canary --team=runtime`

deploy-bot: Feature flag change applied to canary env: `batching_optimizer_enabled=false`

ops-sre: slight improvement in acceptance rate, queue depth down ~25% but still elevated. Some requests still timing out

jm: ok prepare rollback path. Tara, do you want to handoff if we need 1-click rollback?

tara: yes I authorize rollback if we don't see solid improvement in 5 minutes. Support notify: @support-lead can you prep customer comms (holding message ready)?

support-lead: on it. Draft: "We’re investigating elevated API error rates affecting requests in EU region for a small subset of traffic due to a recent canary rollout. No data loss. We may roll back the change shortly. Updates every 15 minutes."

alex.k: still seeing errors, now also increased model load times; p95 model load ~1.4s (was 0.2s)

ops-sre: agreed not safe. Rolling back canary to stable image. Command: `deploy rollback --tag=release/2026-03-08-rc2 --scope=canary --force`

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated for canary pool. Progress: 0/12 nodes -> 4/12 -> 9/12

deploy-bot: Rollback completed for canary pool. All canary nodes now running release/2026-03-08-rc2

ops-sre: monitoring... router queues returning to baseline, p95 latency back to ~0.45s, error rate down to normal

alex.k: confirmed no user-facing errors in top 5 customers, support flagged 3 tickets but all are auto-resolved after rollback (timeouts cleared)

support-lead: sending update to customers now, will include ETA and root-cause notice pending postmortem

tara: good work. quick notes: impact window ~12:05–12:19 UTC, affected ~4.5% of EU requests (canary fraction). No data corruption, no auth exposure. Owner for postmortem: @alex.k, secondary @jm. Assign Sev3 and include rollout trace, kernel/quant logs, and routing metrics.

jm: I'll start collecting traces and the canary config diffs. Recommend we add an automatic preflight check for model load latencies before future canary enrichments.

alex.k: will capture logs + reproduce locally. Adding a follow-up ticket for FF safety gate and a preflight script.

ops-sre: closing the urgent page. If anything resurfaces ping in #eng-oncall and I'll re-open. :white_check_mark:
